As I attended to this wisely, there arose in me the realization of things as they truly are: 'When <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) does not exist, <s>saṃskāras</s> do not come into being. Through the cessation of <s>avidyā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s> cease.'

children.translated_text: That is to say: through the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations);

He would go to the king and report:

body.translated_text: 'May the lord know this: while wandering through a wild forest, I saw an ancient path, an ancient track, an ancient road traveled and followed by people of old. I followed it, and following it I saw an ancient city, an ancient royal capital, endowed with parks, endowed with groves, endowed with lotus ponds, beautiful, wooded, and delightful. May the lord restore that city.' The king would then restore that city, and in time that royal capital would become prosperous, flourishing, secure, abundant in food, and teeming with many people. Even so, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), I have discovered the ancient path, the ancient track, the ancient road traveled and followed by the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) of old.

body.text: katamo 'sau bhikṣavaḥ purāṇo mārgaḥ purāṇaṃ vartma purāṇaṃ paṭumaṃ pūrvakair ṛṣibhir yātānuyātaṃ yad utāryāṣṭāṅgo mārgaḥ tadyathā samyagdṛṣṭiḥ samyaksaṃkalpaḥ samyagvāk* samyakkarmāntaḥ samyagājīvaḥ samyagvyāyāmaḥ samyaksmṛtiḥ samyaksamādhir ayam asau bhikṣavaḥ purāṇo mārgaḥ purāṇaṃ vartma purāṇaṃ paṭumaṃ pūrvakair ṛṣibhir yātānuyātaṃ |
body.translated_text: And what, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, is that ancient path, that ancient track, that ancient road traveled and followed by the <s>ṛṣis</s> of old? It is the <s>Āryāṣṭāṅga Mārga</s> (Noble Eightfold Path), namely: <s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (right view), <s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s> (right intention), <s>samyagvāk</s> (right speech), <s>samyakkarmānta</s> (right action), <s>samyagājīva</s> (right livelihood), <s>samyagvyāyāma</s> (right effort), <s>samyaksmṛti</s> (right mindfulness), <s>samyaksamādhi</s> (right concentration) — this, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, is that ancient path, that ancient track, that ancient road traveled and followed by the <s>ṛṣis</s> of old.

body.text: so 'haṃ tam anugatavān* so 'haṃ tam anugacchaṃ jarāmaraṇam adrākṣaṃ jarāmaraṇasamudayaṃ jarāmaraṇanirodhaṃ jarāmaraṇanirodhagāminīṃ ca pratipadam adrākṣaṃ |
body.translated_text: I followed that path. Following it, I saw <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death), the arising of <s>jarāmaraṇa</s>, the cessation of <s>jarāmaraṇa</s>, and the practice leading to the cessation of <s>jarāmaraṇa</s>.

body.text: jātiṃ bhavam upādānaṃ tṛṣṇāṃ vedanāṃ sparśaṃ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ nāmarūpaṃ vijñānaṃ saṃskārān adrākṣaṃ saṃskārasamudayaṃ saṃskāranirodhaṃ saṃskāranirodhagāminīṃ pratipadam adrākṣaṃ | so 'ham imān dharmāṃ svayam abhijñayābhisaṃbuddhya bhikṣūṇām ārocayāmi bhikṣuṇīnām upāsakānām upāsikānām anyeṣāṃ ca śramaṇabrāhmaṇacarakaparivrājakānām* |
body.translated_text: I saw <s>jāti</s> (birth), <s>bhava</s> (becoming), <s>upādāna</s> (clinging), <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), <s>sparśa</s> (contact), <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (the six sense bases), <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — I saw the arising of <s>saṃskāras</s>, the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>, and the practice leading to the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>. Having realized these <s>dharmas</s> (teachings) by my own direct knowledge, I declare them to <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), <s>upāsakas</s> (male lay followers), <s>upāsikās</s> (female lay followers), and to other <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics), <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (brahmins), <s>carakas</s> (wanderers), and <s>parivrājakas</s> (mendicants).

body.text: tatra bhikṣur api samyakpratipadyamāna ārādhako bhavaty ārādhayati nyāyyaṃ dharmaṃ kuśalaṃ | bhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikās samyakpratipadyamānā ārādhikā bhavaṃty ārādhayanti nyāyyaṃ dharmaṃ kuśalaṃ | evam idaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vaistārikaṃ bāhujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtaṃ yāvad devamanuṣyebhyas samyaksuprakāśitaṃ | tato 'vasāne pariṇāmitaṃ |
body.translated_text: In this regard, a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who practices correctly succeeds and accomplishes the righteous, wholesome <s>dharma</s>. <s>Bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns), <s>upāsakas</s> (male lay followers), and <s>upāsikās</s> (female lay followers) who practice correctly succeed and accomplish the righteous, wholesome <s>dharma</s>. Thus this holy life has become widespread, extensive, well-known, and well-proclaimed to <s>devas</s> (gods) and humans. At the end, the merit was dedicated.

body.translated_text: For the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said: "There are five benefits of being learned (<s>bāhuśrutya</s>). What five? One becomes skilled in the elements (<s>dhātukuśala</s>), skilled in the sense-bases (<s>āyatanakuśala</s>), skilled in dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpādakuśala</s>), skilled in what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthānakuśala</s>), and one's counsel and instruction are not dependent on others." By him, striving, exerting, and endeavoring, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>arhatva</s> (the state of an <s>arhat</s>) was directly realized. He became an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion toward the three realms, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, with a mind like space and the palm of the hand, like a razor and sandalwood, with the egg-shell of ignorance split open, having attained <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge), and <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge), turned away from existence, gain, greed, and honor, and became one worthy of worship, respect, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

body.translated_text: At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was sitting before an assembly of many hundreds of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. But when he realized this, he would live with the well-behaved <s>bhikṣus</s> instead, and except by the Teacher's command, he would come to see them three times daily.
